question.text: The CVaR (Expected Shortfall) at 95% of a portfolio is Rs. 3 cr. This means:

answer.text: The portfolio will lose Rs. 3 cr 95% of the time
Given that losses exceed the 95% VaR, the EXPECTED loss is Rs. 3 cr
There is a 5% probability of losing exactly Rs. 3 cr
The minimum loss at 95% confidence is Rs. 3 cr

explanation.text: The Logic: CVaR = Expected loss conditional on being in the worst 5% of scenarios. Rs. 3 cr is the average loss in that tail — not a threshold. The Trap: '95% of the time' confuses probability vs expectation of losses in the tail. Cross-Exam Context: Core XXI-B. Manager's Pro-Tip: Report both VaR and CVaR to investors — VaR shows the loss threshold, CVaR shows the average pain beyond it.
